text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. Each time this happens, an automated build starts. This means the system checks that the code works and combines it with the rest of the project. During the build, tests run automatically to make sure nothing is broken. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines are the tools that manage these steps. They build, test, and report results quickly. As a result, developers can fix mistakes fast and keep the software in good shape.
